title: Lamp of Our Feet
description: Lamp of Our Feet in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 11 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Bernard Barton, first published in 1826. The tune, ST. AGNES, is by John Bacchus Dykes (1866). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Lamp of our feet! where-by we trace Our path, when wont to stray; Stream from the fount of heav'n-ly grace! Brook by the trav-'ler's way!

lines: Lamp of our feet! whereby we trace
Our path, when wont to stray;
Stream from the fount of heav'nly grace!
Bread of our souls! whereon we feed;
Our guide, and chart wherein we read
When waves would whelm our tossing bark—
Compass! by which our course we keep;
Our shield and buckler in the fight!
Comfort in grief! in weakness, might!
Our hope\-when we go down to dust,
Given forth from Delphos' mystic shrine
Without Thee, how could earth be trod?
Yet to unfold thy hidden worth,
That Spirit which first gave thee forth,
And we, if we aright would learn
Must to its heavenly teaching turn
